questions.prompt: At the Round B tabletop checkpoint, which case material may the learner use for the triage decision?

options.text: R1–R16, with later Round C and D cards still withheld
R1–R24 plus the Branch S report
P1/C1 and V1, because they describe later booking state
The final model answer regardless of its release time

questions.explanation: Round B releases R9–R16 in addition to Round A's R1–R8. R17–R24 and the separate recovery cards are later injects and cannot support the frozen Round B decision.

questions.prompt: A facilitator explores Branch P after students have completed Branch S. How should the alternative be handled?

options.text: Merge Branch S revocation with Branch P's two pending queue requests
Reset to the frozen Round C facts and label Branch P as a separate replay
Treat Branch P as proof that Branch S failed
Use whichever branch has the higher classroom score as canonical fact

questions.explanation: The branches are distinct counterfactual continuations from the same Round C point. Combining their actions and queue facts fabricates a case state that neither branch supplies.

questions.prompt: A six-output tabletop submission scores 8/12, with zero for its recovery plan. Does it meet the chapter's classroom pass rule?

options.text: Yes, because any score above half passes
Yes, because a later good status message can replace the zero
No; the threshold is at least 9/12 and critical zeros require repair
The rubric certifies a real organization's readiness instead

questions.explanation: The original classroom rubric uses two points per output, a 9/12 threshold and no zero for approval or evidence scope. A scored original remains in the record; a revised artifact receives a new version and grade.
questions.source: Chapter 4, Lessons 16 and 20, §§4.5 and 4.23a, rubric and frozen audit

questions.prompt: The V1 synthetic audit lacks an actor identifier. Which after-action item would be measurable?

options.text: Close the issue because the tabletop discussion was strong
Assign an application/audit owner, run a controlled retest for actor and UTC time, and review the resulting evidence
Add a note saying all future audits will be fine
Correct B19 and B20 and assume the audit defect is fixed

questions.explanation: An improvement ticket needs an owner, deadline and observable test. Correcting individual bookings is a separate case action; it does not repair the recurring audit-attribution control.

questions.prompt: At simulated 09:52, M2 forwards an unattributed claim that a newsletter list was stolen. What does M2 establish?

options.text: Confirmed access to the newsletter list
A mandatory public notification duty in a known jurisdiction
Receipt of an unverified statement requiring provenance and a bounded privacy review
Proof that R24's earlier limited observation was false

questions.explanation: M2 lacks the original author, alleged access time and source record. Preserve it as a report of a claim, state its provenance gap and ask the privacy contact and incident lead for an authorized discriminator.

questions.prompt: A tabletop team talks through a recovery plan and earns a high classroom score. What has the exercise actually measured?

options.text: A production restore within the organization's RTO
The participants' reasoning and coordination from supplied fictional records
The identity provider's live revocation behavior
The completeness of every audit source during a real incident

questions.explanation: This is a discussion-based tabletop. It does not contact systems, execute a change or restore a database; a separate authorized functional test is required for operational performance claims.

questions.prompt: An internal incident instruction has a successful channel-delivery receipt. Which state remains unproved by delivery alone?

options.text: That a message reached the declared channel destination
That a dispatch route was used
That the intended role understood the version and read it back correctly
That the channel recorded a delivery event

questions.explanation: Delivery is narrower than role acknowledgement or checked read-back. Each receipt is tied to a message version; neither communication receipt proves a real control was executed or effective.

questions.prompt: A communications contact approves wording about a proposed session restriction. Does that authorize the identity administrator to revoke the session?

options.text: Yes, approved wording is also action approval
Yes, if the recipient later reads the wording back
No; the operational target and conditions need their own accountable approval and receipt
No; a session can never be revoked in an incident

questions.explanation: Approval to communicate governs message wording, audience and channel. Approval to execute governs the operational action, target, duration and conditions; one cannot be inferred from the other.

questions.prompt: What makes the BH4 reconstruction a blind handoff while still permitting valid evidence review?

options.text: The receiver may not open any source material
The sender freezes a version and gives no hints until the receiver's first answer is frozen
The receiver reads the final model answer before writing
The sender rewrites the packet silently as questions arise

questions.explanation: Blind means no off-record explanation from the packet author during the first reconstruction, not withholding the declared permitted source cards. A later clarification and revised version cannot be scored as the original unaided pass.

questions.prompt: EX048 asks for a two-sentence update at the first 09:45 Branch D checkpoint. May it cite V1's blank audit actor?

options.text: Yes, because V1 is printed later in the same book
Yes, if the conclusion would be correct after all cards are released
No; V1 is released later, so freeze the branch-only update first
No; audit observations are never relevant to a handoff

questions.explanation: The first Branch D checkpoint permits the chosen S or P report only. P1/C1 and then V1 arrive in distinct later phases; a later full handoff may cite V1 but must preserve the earlier version.
